axis_notes.hook: Water rising before the phone warning is the right idea. But the first 0.7 s is a dry static yard, the boots and fence mark are tiny, and the flood is a thin mid-frame band over an empty lower half.
axis_notes.story: Clear actor, mechanism, source limit (no field result, no town named) and a performed turn at 41 to 52 s. The close is soft.
axis_notes.picture: Many causally performed actions: charge, sensors submerged, chip signals, risk bar, radio rings, stamp. Against that: repeated 1.5 to 2.6 s holds, a tiny picture-in-picture station inset, floating arms, a closed-eyed operator, and large empty lower-frame areas.
axis_notes.place: Bexar County, blackland. The skyline is generic and the lawn is flat and generic. No Bexar landmark is pictured beyond the tiny editorial map locator. Scored low but not called a county mismatch.
axis_notes.craft: Camera is mostly motivated. Defects: the clipped 'Flash Floo' alert text for about 2.6 s, the enclosure sliding off the left edge at 24 to 25 s, the caption overlapping the map edge at 38.2 to 38.4 s, empty lower thirds.
axis_notes.voice: Provisional. I did not hear audio. Captions are present and match the clause text. Alignment to the final mix is unmeasured by me. This number is not a listening judgment.

attention_review.hook_observed: 0 to 0.7 s: a dry static yard. Water starts rising at 0.8 s and tops the curb and fence by 1.2 s. The boots float by 2.4 s and the county map outline draws from 2.2 s. A hard cut at 4.0 s to a dark phone. The warning arrives at 5.6 s, after the water. The idea is sound, but the subject is small and the lower half of the frame is empty lawn.
attention_review.continuity_observed: The flooded street and curb, the chain-link fence and the skyline recur across the cut at 8.7 s. The pole station carries across 8.7 to 11.5 s, then 11.5 to 15.7 s, then the sensor cut. The same station appears in the street, the country and the inset. The bulletin board and the fence map share the flooded street plate. The 35.4 s operator desk is a new location with no bridge. The desk figure, the woman at 55.5 s and the arm at 52.2 s do not read as one recurring person.

Unearned or near-static intervals: 5.8 to 8.7 s (phone with clipped text, about 2.6 s); 19.8 to 21.6 s (enclosure static while the chip clause is spoken); 29.4 to 31.0 s; 33.4 to 35.4 s; 40.4 to 41.2 s; 41.0 to 42.5 s (empty bar); 43.6 to 46.3 s (slow push only); 54.4 to 55.5 s; 57.4 to 59.4 s (figure static, nothing happening). No reward interval exceeds 4 s. The enclosure setup runs about 5.5 s from 19.8 to 25.3 s with a late push, and the board setting runs 41.0 to 52.1 s with camera moves rather than cuts; whether either breaks the 5 s shot limit depends on declared shot boundaries I could not check. Nothing arrives too fast to follow, but the 18.4 to 19.8 s weather-box labels are held only 1.4 s before the cut.
attention_review.comprehension_observed: One viewing communicates: flood water arrives before the phone warning; a self-powered pole station; sensors that watch the water; an on-chip model that judges risk locally; radio range; a hub map for responders; a university accuracy number; and the source limit (no field result, no town named). Confusions: 'Four optical sensors' is captioned over Rain, Temperature, Humidity and Light labels at 18.4 to 19.1 s; the dashed 'no server' link reads as a loose line; the station inset at 31.2 to 35.3 s is tiny and the rings emanate from the inset rather than the scene's station; 'Deployment is still the goal' is pictured as a plan being put away.
attention_review.remembered_image: The blank 'Field result' card at 49.2 to 51.8 s with the hand stamping 'None reported' beside the 98.82% card. It makes the central claim and its source limit as one picture.
attention_review.weakest_interval: 5.8 to 8.7 s: the phone alert holds static for about 2.6 s with the text clipped to 'Flash Floo' at the phone edge, at the hook's payoff. Repair: resize the banner so the full text fits, add a phone-reaction beat (a ripple on the water or a hand reaching in) or cut at 7.0 s, and start the station cut on the end of the clause.
